The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8e4c129bdb0f2f45), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 26-27. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. statement: Let g be a fixed smooth metric on S3, and fix 0 < t2 < t3 < 1. Assume that g = g∗ on {r ≥ t2}, where g∗ is the unit round metric and r = (x2 1 + x2 2)1/2. Fix an integer B ≥ 1. 26 For every pair of integers k ≥ 0, P ≥ 1, there exist finite integers m∗, D∗, depending only on k, P, B, with the following property. Suppose that, for all sufficiently large integers n, there are real smooth functions Un and positive continuous functions Wn such that |Un| + n−1 |∇Un| ≥ n−B Wn, (4.15) |∇j Un| ≤ Cjnj+4 Wn, |∇j ((∆g + Λn)Un)| ≤ Cjn4−D∗ Wn (0 ≤ j ≤ m∗), (4.16) Un = wn = ℜ(x1 + ix2)n on {r ≥ t2}, (4.17) where all Cj are independent of n. Then, for all sufficiently large n, there are a smooth Riemannian metric b gn and a positive smooth function e vn on S3 such that, with un = Un/e vn, (∆b gn + Λn)un = 0, ∥b gn − g∥Ck ≤ n−P , (4.18) b gn = g∗, e vn = 1, un = wn on {r ≥ t3}. (4.19) In particular un is nonzero and has exactly the same pointwise signs and zero set as Un. The threshold for n may depend on the fixed input data and on the constants in (4.16).
